_note: Written BEFORE any reader saw a line (row IC, Session 4b, IC4-R1). `pairs` is the plan's question 1 (two lines, two named marshals: which said which); `sixway` the harder test besides. The confused pairings (Ney/Lannes, Massena/Davout) drawn twice each.

who.Ney: Ney — a bold marshal, famous for his courage and his impatience to fight.
who.Davout: Davout — a careful marshal, strict, exact, who counts every man and never wastes one.
who.Murat: Murat — a bold cavalry marshal who loves to ride and charge.
who.Lannes: Lannes — a bold marshal who marches to the sound of the guns and leads assaults himself.
who.Massena: Masséna — a stubborn marshal who never gives up ground he holds.
who.Bernadotte: Bernadotte — a slow, politic marshal who is never in a hurry and always has an excuse.

pairs.line1: My own judgement, Sire? Then I march to the guns.
pairs.line2: No task, Sire? I'll find a fight myself now, before I go mad sitting here.

pairs.line1: It went badly, Sire. Give me another go; I'd sooner be fighting than brooding.
pairs.line2: I failed, Sire. Straight talk: I'll lead the assault again.

pairs.line1: Give me a post, Sire, with the rolls and stores to match. I'll see every man fed.
pairs.line2: Let me hold my front, Sire, and strike out from it when I see the chance.

pairs.line1: A quiet day on my front. It stays my front.
pairs.line2: I waited, Sire, and counted. The rolls are right.

pairs.line1: Quiet for the moment. I'm listening for the guns.
pairs.line2: No news from my part of the line, Sire. Let's hope it stays that way.

pairs.line1: Set me one task, Sire. I'll carry it out with every man counted, and you can judge.
pairs.line2: Give me a task, Sire, and I'll lead the assault myself.

pairs.line1: You overruled me once, Sire. I've not forgotten — but I'll go now.
pairs.line2: I was recalled once in the middle of a chase. I've not forgotten it.

pairs.line1: I'll hold here if I must, Sire, but I'm restless. Let me loose the moment something shows.
pairs.line2: I could hold where I am, Sire. Quiet work, and safe.

pairs.line1: I'll not do the same thing a third day, Sire. A fixed habit wastes men.
pairs.line2: Bored of this, Sire. The horses and I have changed it.

pairs.line1: I've changed it, Sire. I'll stay on what is mine, but not like that.
pairs.line2: Bored of this, Sire. The horses and I have changed it.

pairs.line1: After that, Sire, I'm going very carefully indeed.
pairs.line2: A bad day for the cavalry. It makes me think twice.

pairs.line1: My own judgement, Sire. Nobody takes a yard from me, and I'll take theirs.
pairs.line2: As I see fit, Sire? I'll weigh it all carefully first, I'm sure you understand.

rows.line: Every man was in place, so I sent them in, Sire.
I went out from my lines today, Sire.
I attacked, as it happens, Sire. I hope you understand it could not be helped.
We were up with the guns, in the thick of it, Sire.
I did not wait, Sire. You know I never do.
I led the charge myself, Sire, plume and all.
Then I ride wherever the enemy is, Sire.
Leave it to me, Sire. I'm moving now, and quickly.
Very good, Sire. I'll move when the moment is right, and not before.
As I see fit, Sire. Wherever the guns are loudest, that's where you'll find me.
My own judgement, Sire. Nobody takes a yard from me, and I'll take theirs.
As I see fit, Sire. I'll count what I have, then strike where it pays.
Give me one ride to prove myself, Sire.
Give me a task, Sire, and I'll lead the assault myself.
Let me have one task, Sire, to show my good faith.
One task, Sire. Whatever I take is mine, and I'll bring you more.
Give me one task, Sire, and soon. I can't bear the waiting.
Give me a task and a few turns, Sire. Nothing will be wasted, neither men nor days.
It went badly, Sire. Give me another go; I'd sooner be fighting than brooding.
The ride did not go as I pictured it, Sire.
I failed this once, Sire. I held my ground to the last, and I'll not be judged by it.
I failed, Sire. Straight talk: I'll lead the assault again.
It was not enough. I'll check the rolls, Sire, and do it right.
It did not succeed, Sire. Circumstances were against me.
I must say I have doubts, Sire. I'll go, slowly.
You want me to sit and watch them, Sire? I'll do it, and I won't like it.
I don't like leaving a place I've made mine, Sire. I'll go if I must.
Plainly, Sire: this is a mistake. I'll do it, but my ear stays on the guns.
Sit still, Sire? Horsemen are made to ride.
I'll do it if you insist, Sire. The figures are worse than they look.
